title: First Search for Ultraheavy Dark Matter Using a Magnetically Levitated Particle
authors: Dennis G. Uitenbroek, Dorian W. P. Amaral, Juehang Qin, Jurriaan Langendorff, Andrew Gingerich, Tjerk H. Oosterkamp, Christopher D. Tunnell
abstract: We present the first search for ultraheavy dark matter using a magnetically levitated particle. The POLONAISE experiment uses a milligram-scale ferromagnet levitated in a superconducting trap, admitting a force sensitivity of $0.07\,\mathrm{fN\,Hz^{-1/2}}$ and resolving impulses as small as $1\,\mathrm{TeV}/c$. Treating every candidate impulse as a possible dark matter event, we set optimum-interval upper limits on the neutron coupling $α_n$ for dark matter interacting through a new light mediator. For dark matter masses $10^6\,\mathrm{GeV}/c^2\text{-}10^{15}\,\mathrm{GeV}/c^2$ and mediators lighter than $30\,\mathrm{meV}/c^2$, we exclude couplings as low as $α_n = 3.2\times 10^{-9}$ at $95\%$ confidence level and set leading constraints on the dark matter-neutron cross section for composite dark matter. Our results extend levitated sensing beyond the mass reach of optical levitation by seven orders of magnitude into the ultraheavy dark matter frontier.
summary: This work reports on the first search for ultraheavy dark matter using a magnetically levitated particle detector. By analyzing minute impulses, the experiment sets world-leading upper limits on the coupling strength between dark matter and neutrons. This technique significantly extends the reach for UHDM detection into mass regimes inaccessible to previous methods.
main_problem: The paper presents the first search for ultraheavy dark matter (UHDM) by detecting the impulse imparted by such particles on a magnetically levitated particle.
main_result: The experiment sets stringent upper limits on the dark matter-neutron coupling ($\alpha_n$) for UHDM masses in the range $10^6$ to $10^{15}$ GeV/$c^2$, extending sensitivity significantly beyond previous optical levitation methods.
method: The analysis uses a magnetically levitated ferromagnet in a superconducting trap, monitoring minute impulses in its motion using a SQUID readout and applying an optimum-interval statistical test.
model_or_system: The physical system is a milligram-scale ferromagnet levitated in a superconducting trap, which acts as a highly sensitive detector for external forces. The interaction is modeled via a Yukawa-like potential mediated by a light boson ($\phi$) coupling to neutrons.
key_observables: Impulse magnitude ($q$), coupling strength ($\alpha_n$), and the resulting exclusion limits on $\alpha_n$ vs. DM mass ($m_{	ext{DM}}$).
important_parameters: Noise floor ($0.07 	ext{ fN } 	ext{Hz}^{-1/2}$), momentum threshold ($1 	ext{ TeV}/c$), and the mediator mass range ($< 30 	ext{ meV}/c^2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the DM interaction is point-like and that the signal is detectable above classical noise sources, extending sensitivity where optical methods fail.
figures_summary: Figures show the 95% CL limits on the DM–neutron coupling $\alpha_n$ versus DM mass $m_{	ext{DM}}$ for various mediator masses, and the constraint on the DM-neutron cross-section ($\sigma_{\chi n}$) derived from fifth-force bounds.
paper_structure: The paper details the experimental setup (POLONAISE), the theoretical framework for DM interaction (Yukawa potential), the data analysis techniques (optimum-interval method on transient impulses), and finally presents the derived exclusion limits on DM couplings and cross-sections.
why_interesting: While the primary focus is particle astrophysics, the core methodology relies on ultra-sensitive force detection and noise characterization of mechanical oscillators, which has parallels with advanced sensing techniques used in AMO physics.
